🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Huachicol Fiscal: Senate Sets Fines of Up to 100% of the Cargo's Value</u>

The Senate approved the president's Customs Law reform 66–37, over opposition protests. Fuel and petroleum imports with irregular paperwork will now be fined 50% to 100% of their commercial value. The reform also scraps the 50% threshold that kept customs from seizing undervalued shipments when the price gap was smaller. It takes effect January 1, 2027.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexico and the US Freeze a Cártel del Noreste Network That Funded Election Campaigns</u>

Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF) and the US Treasury acted together: the bank accounts and assets of four people and 11 companies tied to the Cártel del Noreste are now frozen. The businesses ranged from quarter-horse racing to construction, trucking, and oil and gas. According to OFAC, one of them, Construcciones y Edificaciones Garza Elías (Cegesa), funneled cartel money into election campaigns and won government contracts through corruption.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Yucatán Draws 11.6 Billion Pesos in Tourism Investment, and Most of It Skips Mérida</u>

Yucatán has captured 11,566 million pesos in tourism investment since Governor Joaquín Díaz Mena took office, in projects tied to 15,508 jobs (4,810 direct), El Economista reports from the state tourism ministry's data. 59.2% of it, 6,851 million pesos, is going to the interior of the state rather than Mérida, the towns the Tren Maya was built to connect. Accumulated investment grew by 2,952 million pesos in the last year alone.

🇲🇽✊ <u>Mexico City's Labor Center Wins 2.9 Billion Pesos for Workers</u>

Mexico City's Labor Conciliation Center has recovered more than 2,896 million pesos for workers in 2026, Labor Secretary Inés González Nicolás reported. It serves about 1,500 people a day, mostly over unjustified dismissals, unpaid benefits and missing Social Security registration, and settles disputes in 45 days at most without going to court. Under the old conciliation and arbitration boards that the 2019 labor reform abolished, workers waited years.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>IMSS Takes Worker Complaints to All 277 Hospitals, With Deadlines and Names</u>

After IMSS workers and retirees protested in 12 states, director Zoé Robledo announced listening sessions in all 277 second- and third-level hospitals, where more than 267,000 people work, starting with the high-specialty units. Eight issues are on the table, from medical supplies and prescriptions to staffing and equipment. Every demand has to become a commitment with three parts: which problem gets fixed first, a deadline, and a named person responsible.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's Crackdown in Numbers: 569 Tons of Drugs, 2,792 Labs Dismantled</u>

Trump and the opposition keep saying Mexico isn't doing enough against the cartels. The Security Cabinet's tally from October 2024 to September 30, 2026: more than 70,500 arrests for high-impact crimes, 36,300 firearms and 569 tons of drugs seized, and 2,792 clandestine synthetic-drug labs dismantled. On October 12 alone, the Navy intercepted a boat carrying about 1.2 tons of cocaine 366 nautical miles south of Huatulco, Oaxaca.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Jalisco Governor Frees All 39 Water Protesters and Admits Police Excess</u>

After student blockades on Periférico Norte, a sit-in outside the government palace and demands from Morena and President Sheinbaum, Jalisco's MC governor Pablo Lemus announced that all 39 people detained at Sunday's march against contaminated water are free. After reviewing the footage, he admitted the operation got out of control, with excessive force and unjust arrests, and said neither water cannons nor gas should have been used. Some 15,000 people had marched over tap water arriving with heavy metals, fecal matter and worms.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>8.4 Trillion Pesos: Mexico's Biggest Public Investment Push Ever</u>

At the 50th anniversary of the business council CCE, President Sheinbaum put a number on her infrastructure plan: 8.4 trillion pesos in public and mixed investment through 2030, about 23% of Mexico's 2025 GDP, and that's before counting private capital. Roughly 3 trillion goes to Bienestar housing, 2 trillion to Pemex's strategic plan, 794 billion to power generation and 180 billion to water projects. In her words, an amount "never before seen in a sexenio."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico Scraps 10% Auto-Parts Tariff for Five Years to Bring Assembly Lines Home</u>

A decree from President Sheinbaum, published in the DOF on October 13, removes the 10% tariff on imported parts and components for car assembly for five years, starting October 14. It covers automakers with bonded-warehouse authorization that follow Economy Ministry rules (tariff line 9803.00.01). The decree's stated goal is to build in Mexico the light vehicles the country now imports and to grow local suppliers under Plan México, El Financiero reports. Mexican-built cars still pay a 25% tariff to enter the US, compared with 15% for Japan and the EU.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Swiss Firms Plan 4 Billion Francs of Investment in Mexico Through 2030</u>

Swiss companies operating in Mexico plan to invest about 4 billion Swiss francs between 2025 and 2030, in step with Plan México, the Swiss-Mexican Chamber of Commerce (SwissCham México) announced. Swiss firms already support roughly 60,000 jobs in the country. The chamber pointed to Mexico's domestic market, its export manufacturing capacity and its integrated supply chains, while Mexico and Switzerland are updating their EFTA trade agreement, now 25 years old.
